html:
SMTO-HTTP-0081 — The service refused access for this account

GUID: af630d5e-e8f6-4a87-915f-77699dc0a798
Slug: http-auth-access-denied
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service's sign-in check refused access for this account. That doesn't mean the password is wrong; the account may not be allowed to use this part of the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who runs the service to check that this account has the permissions or role needed for what SMTO is doing. The service recognized the request but chose not to allow it, which is usually an account permission setting.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the connection, and check that it uses the account you meant, and for OAuth that Scopes lists the access you need. A connection set to a different account, or asking for too little access, is refused even with correct details.
  3. After the owner changes the account's access, select Test connection. The test confirms the service now lets this account in.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Reachable and Authenticated, and the task can use the connection.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the service owner. Don't change the password or turn off certificate checks just because of this message; neither fixes an access refusal.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The authentication endpoint returned HTTP 403, an access rejection that does not by itself show the credential is incorrect.

What this means

  • HTTP 403 establishes that the authentication endpoint rejected access. Account policy, scope, role or authentication-method restrictions can produce this response even when a credential is valid. The status alone does not establish which condition applies.

Why this can happen

  • The endpoint denied access; its authorization rules and account state determine the underlying reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Confirm the intended account, endpoint, required scopes or roles and authentication method with the service owner. Replace credentials only if a separate check establishes that they are invalid.

How to fix it

  • auth_http_failure maps the 403 to http_credentials_rejected and the resolver refines it to http_auth_access_denied. Have the service owner check the account's scopes, roles and endpoint access policy; rotate credentials only if credential invalidity is separately established, and do not weaken TLS.
  • Ask the service owner to check the intended account, scopes, roles and endpoint access policy. Reauthenticate only if credential invalidity is separately established.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account is accepted by the authentication endpoint under the required access policy.

What not to do

  • Do not rotate credentials or weaken TLS solely because the provider returned HTTP 403.

Technical notes

  • The resolver refines http_credentials_rejected only when retained status is 403; status and execution behavior are unchanged.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-HTTP-0037 — The service didn't accept SMTO's sign-in
  • SMTO-HTTP-0038 — SMTO couldn't find the service's sign-in address
  • SMTO-HTTP-0044 — SMTO couldn't confirm the service's security certificate
